issues.diagnosis: CI clicked immediately after an asynchronously loaded preview. The final DOM had a disabled install button and no install request. Current implementation resets consent in a preview-hash effect; the original test did not establish that effect completion or assert readiness after consent. Local bounded reproductions did not recreate this failure, so a browser production defect is not claimed.
issues.repair: Explicit async act completes the immediate fixture preview interaction, then readiness is awaited after consent. Retains disabled-before-consent and exact previewHash checks; adds a disabled-button no-dispatch assertion. Applies the same interaction boundary to original-receipt recovery test.

issues.diagnosis: Total operation count includes pending records. createOperation publishes count 2 before updateOperation publishes the completed set through a separate asynchronous IDB read. The prior test waited for total count, not the newly completed result.
issues.repair: Separately assert the two-record/one-completed pending state, then await two-completed state. Verify consent revoked, clear button disabled, disabled click retains both records.

issues.diagnosis: Reproduced Fetch bad port with ephemeral loopback server. Host TCP dynamic port range is 1024-15000, which intersects the Fetch forbidden-port list. This is distinct from the CI native worker exit.
issues.repair: Use node:http with test-owned connections, no shared keep-alive pool and bounded timeout. Preserve all 15 real HTTP/raw TCP/WebSocket tests and assertions; no skip/retry/filter added.

nativeWorkerExit.evidence: Same-head PR CI in .work/v220-ci1-pr-windows-raw.txt passed this file. Before changes, two Node versions plus 14 bounded exact-file repeats never reproduced this worker exit (one repeat exposed the separate forbidden-port failure). No process-targeting or native child-process use exists in the preview fixture/test. This does not prove a native crash cause or fix.
nativeWorkerExit.gate: Next complete CI must execute this entire file and treat any worker error as failure; no exception or retry acceptance.
